chapter_title: Center of Mass, Momentum, and Collisions

canonical_taxonomy_mapping.chapter_name: Center of Mass and Linear Momentum

topics.title: Center of Mass Calculation and System Dynamics

subtopics.title: Center of Mass of Discrete Particle Systems
subtopics.description: Weighted average position vector R_cm = sum(m_i r_i) / sum(m_i); Cartesian coordinate components x_cm, y_cm, z_cm; two-particle internal division ratio r1/r2 = m2/m1.

subtopics.title: Center of Mass of Continuous Bodies via Integration
subtopics.description: Volume/surface/linear density mass element formulation dm = rho dV = sigma dA = lambda dl; integral formulation R_cm = 1/M int r dm; standard symmetric geometries: uniform rod (L/2), semicircular ring (2R/pi), semicircular disc (4R/3pi), solid hemisphere (3R/8), hollow hemisphere (R/2), solid cone (h/4), hollow cone (h/3).

subtopics.title: Motion of Center of Mass and System Newton's Law
subtopics.description: Time differentiation yielding V_cm = sum(m_i v_i) / M = P_total / M; acceleration A_cm = sum(m_i a_i) / M; internal cancellation by Newton's Third Law sum(F_int) = 0; governing dynamical theorem M A_cm = F_net,ext.

subtopics.title: Shift in Center of Mass and Cavity Problems
subtopics.description: Negative mass superposition method for bodies with holes/cavities; shift in center of mass when parts of an isolated system relocate (Delta X_cm = 0 under zero external horizontal force); man-on-plank and boat-shore problems.

topics.title: Linear Momentum, Impulse, and Variable Mass Systems

subtopics.title: Conservation of Linear Momentum
subtopics.description: System linear momentum P = M V_cm; constancy dP/dt = F_net,ext = 0 implying P_initial = P_final for isolated systems; directional conservation along unconstrained axes; explosion of projectiles and gun recoil dynamics.

subtopics.title: Impulse and the Impulse-Momentum Theorem
subtopics.description: Definition of impulse vector J = int F dt; impulse-momentum theorem J_net = Delta p; area under force-time F-t curves; distinction between impulsive forces (tensions, normal impacts, explosions) and finite non-impulsive forces (gravity, gentle spring forces) over infinitesimal impact durations.

subtopics.title: Variable Mass Systems and Rocket Propulsion
subtopics.description: Differential momentum balance for open systems acquiring or ejecting mass; relative exhaust velocity v_rel; reactive thrust force F_thrust = v_rel * (dm/dt); Tsiolkovsky rocket equation v(t) = v_0 + v_rel ln(m_0 / m(t)) - g t; sand leaking on conveyor belts and railcars.

topics.title: Collisions in One and Two Dimensions

subtopics.title: One-Dimensional Head-On Elastic Collisions
subtopics.description: Simultaneous conservation of linear momentum and total mechanical kinetic energy; relative speed of separation equals relative speed of approach; closed-form post-collision velocities v1, v2; velocity exchange for equal masses m1 = m2; heavy target and heavy projectile limiting cases.

subtopics.title: One-Dimensional Inelastic Collisions and Energy Dissipation
subtopics.description: Momentum conserved with kinetic energy partially transformed into internal thermal/deformation energy; formula for kinetic energy loss Delta K = 1/2 * (m1 m2)/(m1 + m2) * (1 - e^2) * (u1 - u2)^2; maximum energy loss in perfectly inelastic collision.

subtopics.title: Completely Inelastic Collisions and Ballistic Pendulum
subtopics.description: Colliding bodies coalesce and move with common velocity v_f = V_cm; ballistic pendulum energy conversion and swing height measurement.

subtopics.title: Coefficient of Restitution and Newton's Experimental Law
subtopics.description: Definition e = v_sep / v_app along line of impact; limits e = 1 (elastic), 0 < e < 1 (inelastic), e = 0 (perfectly inelastic); multi-bounce geometric damping off flat floors.

subtopics.title: Two-Dimensional Oblique Collisions
subtopics.description: Separation of dynamics into Line of Impact (common normal) and Line of Contact (common tangent); normal impulse changes normal momentum governed by restitution e; smooth surfaces imply zero tangential impulse so tangential velocity components remain invariant; 90 degree scattering angle for identical elastic spheres with stationary target.

explicit_exclusions.topic: Rigid Body Rotational Dynamics and Moment of Inertia
explicit_exclusions.rationale: Rotational kinetic energy, moment of inertia tensors, torque tau = I alpha, and angular momentum L = I omega belong to Chapter 6: Rotational Motion.

explicit_exclusions.topic: Universal Gravitation and Two-Body Orbital Mechanics
explicit_exclusions.rationale: Keplerian orbits, reduced mass in central gravitational fields, and escape velocity belong to Chapter 7: Gravitation.
Four-momentum p_mu and Lorentz transformations belong to advanced Modern Physics / Relativity outside classical JEE syllabus.
